item.title: MFA Boston Denies Targeting DEI Staff in Cutbacks, Former French Culture Minister Jack Lang Stepping Down: Morning Links for February 9, 2026
item.description: Here's what we're reading this morning, folks.

item.title: Dreaming of Creating a Giant Public Artwork With Google? Artist Judy Chicago Doesn’t Recommend It.
item.description: In a new essay, the artist said a major commission from the tech company was a disaster.

item.title: Debbie Harry, Georgia O’Keeffe, and Al Green Appear in New Factory Images Acquired by the Smithsonian
item.description: The Smithsonian’s Archives of American Art has acquired more than 400 rarely seen images taken by Ronnie Cutrone, Andy Warhol's longtime assistant.

item.title: Meet the Speakerhead Wiring the Art World for Sound
item.description: Devon Turnbull, a.k.a. OJAS, talks about his listening room at the Cooper Hewitt Smithsonian Design Museum.

item.title: Ai Weiwei Says London’s Royal Academy Sought to Eject Him After Post–October 7 Tweet about Jews
item.description: The artist talked about censorship in his native China as well as the West in an interview with The Guardian.

item.title: Long Misidentified, Object in Museum Is Oldest Drilling Tool Found Yet in Egypt
item.description: Egyptians used sophisticated tools much earlier than previously thought.

item.title: Political Bribery Investigation in South Korea Involving Lee Ufan Painting Draws to a Close
item.description: The former chief prosecutor was acquitted of graft charges related to the painting.

item.title: First Art Basel Qatar Closed with Institutional Acquisitions, Mid-Market Strength, and Measured Sales Momentum
item.description: Wael Shawky framed it succinctly: “Art Basel Qatar has presented a new way forward for the art market.” Whether that way forward means smaller more focused editions of other Art Basel fairs or just that the inaugural Basel Doha was proof that western galleries can sell art in the Middle East is unclear.

item.title: Michaels Sues Artist Who Claimed the Craft Store Giant Used His Work Without Permission
item.description: Jordan Nickel says the DIY chain had no right to use his work.

item.title: British Museum Raises $4.8 M. to Keep ‘Tudor Heart’ Pendant in UK
item.description: Discovered in 2019, the pendant is currently on view at the British Museum.
